studies.label: Randomized two-stage narrative-writing experiment; setting subtype not stated

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 2.1 (valid cases before model-specific exclusions; see notes)
counts_source.quote:
Following data screening for attrition and non-compliance, 112 valid cases remained, resulting in a total
of 224 creative writing samples (first and final drafts combined).

arms.name: AI-first
arms.description: AI-assisted first draft followed by independent final drafting; the first draft could be consulted but not directly modified (PDF pp. 4, 6-7).

arms.name: AI-follow
arms.description: Independent first draft followed by final drafting with freely chosen generative AI tools (PDF pp. 4, 6-7).

arms.name: AI-parallel
arms.description: Generative AI available for both first and final drafting stages (PDF pp. 4, 6-7).

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Both drafts written independently without AI assistance (PDF pp. 4, 6-7).

studies.task: Write a first and final narrative draft on "Imagine and depict the future world", with a separate time limit for each stage.

ai_tool.name: Participant-selected generative AI tools; examples given are ChatGPT and DeepSeek; versions not specified.
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.2.1; PDF p. 7, Section 2.4

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the complete paper; PDF p. 4 describes the study as exploratory.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Ten trained undergraduate raters, blind to condition, independently evaluated each narrative. Originality, fluency, flexibility and elaboration were each rated on a 9-point scale (1 = very poor, 9 = very good); the exact aggregation into overall creativity is not specified (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 2.3-2.3.1). Reported arm levels are ANCOVA-adjusted means and their SEs, not SDs.

sources.quote:
Human-only group achieved a significantly higher adjusted mean score (M = 
5.65, SE = 0.10)

AI-follow group (M = 4.81, SE = 
0.10)
AI-follow by 1.41 standard deviations (p < .001, d = -1.41)

estimates.notes: This is the planned AI-follow versus Human-only contrast from the joint four-arm final-draft ANCOVA (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 2.5). It adjusts for first-draft score, age, gender, AI literacy, and creative personality. Rule 5 is applied per contrast: both arms in this contrast wrote their first drafts independently before AI-follow received AI assistance (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). Thus their first-draft covariate is pre-AI-exposure. The same fitted model also contains AI-first and AI-parallel participants whose first drafts were AI-assisted; this joint-model limitation is retained explicitly and is not treated as an unadjusted effect. The Cohen's d standardizer is not stated. No SD, pairwise test statistic, effect SE or effect CI is printed. The omnibus F test is not entered as the pairwise test. Exact post-exclusion total and per-arm analysis counts are not printed; no counts are reconstructed from exclusions or degrees of freedom. The analysis uses one final-draft score per participant; participant is the uncertainty basis. Section 3.2 calls this a robust ANCOVA but does not specify the robust SE estimator. Seven influential cases were excluded (PDF p. 8, Section 3.2).

estimates.outcome: Final-draft overall narrative creativity (DeepSeek-V3 robustness evaluation)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: DeepSeek-V3 evaluated the participant-written narratives as an automated robustness check. The narrative protocol evaluates originality, fluency, flexibility and elaboration on a 9-point scale; the exact overall-score aggregation is not specified (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 2.3-2.3.2). Reported arm means and SEs are from the repeated final-draft ANCOVA (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3). DeepSeek-V3 is the evaluator, not a standardized treatment tool.

estimates.outcome: Final-draft originality (evaluator unspecified for numerical ANCOVA)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality is defined as novelty and uniqueness of ideas; rated on a 9-point scale (1 = very poor, 9 = very good; PDF p. 5, Section 2.3). Section 3.4 does not identify which evaluator supplies the numerical ANCOVA results. Human and DeepSeek-V3 subscale distributions are separately plotted in Figures 3 and 4 (PDF pp. 18-19), so the numerical result is not assigned to either evaluator.

estimates.outcome: First-draft overall narrative creativity (human ratings; figure only)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Ten trained undergraduate raters independently scored each narrative, blind to condition (PDF p. 6, Section 2.3.1). The protocol rates originality, fluency, flexibility and elaboration on a 9-point scale (1 = very poor, 9 = very good; PDF p. 5, Section 2.3). The overall-score aggregation is not specified. First-draft distributions are shown in Figure 1, without printed arm values or pairwise statistics.

sources.quote:
Comparison of mean creativity scores between first and final drafts across four experimental groups
(Human evaluation). The four groups are: AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel, and Human-only.

estimates.notes: Eligible first-draft output retained as a figure-only record. All outcome statistics are null: the box plot has no numerical labels for arm summaries or pairwise contrasts, and values were not estimated from its axes or points. The valid-case sample counts in Section 2.1 are not explicitly identified as the sample of this particular figure, so estimate-level counts remain null. Section 2.5 (PDF p. 7) mentions a significant first-draft omnibus ANOVA but gives no F statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, or numerical pairwise result. No omnibus result is assigned to this pairwise comparison. AI-first and AI-parallel used AI for first drafts, while Human-only did not (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 2.4). This is a between-person contrast of randomly assigned schedules, not a paired or randomized-order crossover; within_person is null. First-draft production occurred in the initial stage of the same task.

open_items: Randomized assignment is explicit, but the paper does not identify laboratory, online, or ordinary-coursework delivery. design_class is null rather than guessing the RCT subtype. Study country is not explicitly stated (PDF pp. 4-7).
Original randomized total, randomized arm counts and initial attrition/non-compliance losses are not printed (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1).

Exact final-draft analysis totals and per-arm counts after model-specific influential-case exclusions are not printed. The human overall analysis excludes seven cases and the AI-rated analysis excludes eight; subdomain exclusion counts are absent. No totals are calculated (PDF pp. 7-9).
First-draft arm summaries, dispersion and pairwise results are not printed. Figure-specific sample counts are not provided, so figure-only records retain null counts and statistics (PDF pp. 16-19).
Outcome SDs, pairwise effect SEs/CIs, and the standardizer for the reported Cohen's d are not given. Adjusted-mean SEs must not be treated as SDs (PDF pp. 8-9).
The evaluator for Section 3.4 numerical subdomain analyses is not identified; measure is null for these estimates even though both human and DeepSeek-V3 subscale figures exist.

Rule 5 is applied to the exposure history of the contrasted arms: AI-follow versus Human-only has AI-free first drafts in both arms and is retained. Its results nevertheless come from a shared four-arm model whose first-draft covariate is post-AI in the other two arms. A separately fitted two-arm or unadjusted numerical contrast is not printed; this analytic limitation should remain visible in reconciliation.
The paper does not specify the participant treatment-tool versions, their release years, or the distribution of tools actually chosen (PDF pp. 5, 7, 11).
How ratings across evaluators and dimensions are combined into overall narrative creativity is not specified (PDF pp. 5-6).

notes: Extraction B, 2026-10-11. The full markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks, including references, all figure captions and the supplementary-file list. PDF tables/figures and the outcome results were inspected before the design was checked; every numerical estimate was confirmed with pymupdf text extraction. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. Figures 1-5 were rendered in memory and inspected without creating files. Table 1 contains demographic variables only; there is no outcome-statistics table or internal appendix. The outcome-statistic inventory is covered by the numerical estimates and the not_extracted entries. Six numerical final-draft AI-follow contrasts are retained, plus twenty first-draft figure-only records whose effect statistics are entirely null. The figure-only records do not imply evidence of no difference. No AI-configuration pairwise contrast or combined-AI-arm contrast is numerically reported, and none is derived. No across-people diversity outcome is measured. Thematic flexibility refers to categories within a narrative. AI-first final drafts are immediate independent work after AI use, with the AI-assisted first draft still available as a reference; their reported adjusted effects are excluded for post-treatment adjustment. The design is between-person randomization to assistance schedules, not a paired crossover. The screening form and citation record were used as maps and checked against the saved version. The screening data-availability record reports prior access to supplementary participant scores, but that report is not treated as independently confirmed source data for this extraction. PDF p. 20 lists DataSPSS.sav and researchtools.pdf as external supplements; neither is embedded. The researchtools.pdf link and the Research Square publisher fallback both failed in this run using urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. No supplement was used. Counts: PDF p. 4, Section 2.1 reports 112 valid cases and 224 first/final draft samples. These are not post-exclusion final-model denominators. The printed valid-case arm counts are AI-first 28, AI-follow 25, AI-parallel 30 and Human-only 29 (same section); all study/arm n_analyzed fields remain null because the model-specific counts are not supplied. Section 2.5 (PDF p. 7) reports five participants with missing values, five MICE datasets, and N = 112 before model-specific Cook's Distance exclusions. The narrative task allowed 15 minutes per stage (PDF p. 6, Section 2.4). The one-week evaluator retest does not establish any delayed participant outcome. All transcribed numeric precision and signs are preserved in the verbatim sources; trailing zeroes may not be retained by JSON numeric serialization.
